name: DCM Pacific 1985: Red Tide
seed: Bungalow's Dynamic Campaign Pacific 1985: Red Tide
description:
4 May 1985, 0000 Zulu. For three weeks the Pacific Fleet has been at sea on manoeuvres, and the Americans have watched it as they always do, without alarm. Tonight the manoeuvres end. Within the hour the first missiles will fall on Kadena and Ching Chuan Kang; by first light Chinese landing ships will be on the beaches of southern Taiwan.

The plan was drawn in Moscow and in Beijing together, and it is simple. Strike while the enemy sleeps. Take Taiwan, then Okinawa, then Korea, then the Philippines, and last the straits of the south, before America can bring its strength across the Pacific. The Seventh Fleet is in harbour: Midway alongside at Yokosuka, Constellation at Subic Bay, the Marines' ships at White Beach. Our submarines already lie across the lanes from Pearl Harbor, and the missile submarines are safe in the Sea of Okhotsk.

The landing forces are loaded and at sea. The South Sea Fleet's landing squadron, with the 1st Marine Brigade aboard, is a few hours off Tsoying; the Pacific Fleet Landing Group, with the 55th Naval Infantry and Minsk's group around it, is two days from Okinawa.

You command the combined fleets in the Pacific. Take the islands, cut the sea lanes, and break the carriers when they come. The war ends when one side's will to fight breaks, or at the peace table: every base we take, every ship we sink and every lane we cut wears the enemy's will down, and every one we lose wears down ours.

cableTap.name: Guam
cableTap.story: The American command on Guam talks to Pearl Harbor over a cable that runs west of the island. One of our boats can lay a tap on it.

texts.guideWar: 4 May 1985, H-hour. The Soviet Union and China strike first, without warning: Taiwan, Okinawa, South Korea, the Philippines and the straits of the south are to be taken before America can reinforce across the Pacific. You command the combined fleets: the Soviet Pacific Fleet with its Cam Ranh squadron, and the PLA Navy's North, East and South Sea Fleets.
texts.guideWarTask: Two landing forces are already at sea and loaded: the South Sea Fleet's for Tsoying, a few hours out, and the Pacific Fleet's for White Beach on Okinawa, two days out. Your first task is to put them ashore; then take the rest of the island chain, and hold it against the American counter-stroke.
texts.guideExampleMove: The Missile Cruiser Brigade holds east of Honshu. Right-click the sea south of Yokosuka: it plots a sea route and shows its arrival time at each waypoint.
texts.guideExampleSplit: Split the Krivak Revnostny off the Pacific Fleet Landing Group to escort a convoy into White Beach once it is ours, then merge her back when the convoy is safely in.
texts.guideLift: Battalions ride in landing ships: Ivan Rogov, Ropucha, Alligator and the Chinese Yukan 2 each (the enemy's: Tarawa 3, Austin 2, Charleston or Newport 1).
texts.guideLiftIslands: Select the group and right-click an enemy port, or an island airfield with no port (Wake, Midway, Kwajalein).
texts.guideExampleInvade: The Pacific Fleet Landing Group carries 8 battalions (Ivan Rogov, Aleksandr Nikolayev, BDK-101 and BDK-98, 2 each). White Beach, a naval base, is held by a garrison of 3: bring gun escorts, whose fire adds up to 50 %, and strike its field first.
texts.guideDeckRates: the Kiev and the Orel 8; the enemy's Midway 6, Forrestal, Kitty Hawk and America 8, Enterprise and Nimitz 10
texts.guideExampleCarrier: Minsk loses 4 Yak-38s over the Ryukyus. Her open places fill only with aircraft flown aboard: order Yak-38s at a field in her reach, then REBASE them to her, or give a flight Land at… her. Her Ka-27s, once lost, are lost for good. Her magazine refills in port at a naval base, from its aviation stores.
texts.guideReplen: Your side starts with none. The Kazbek (fuel) and the Boris Chilikin (fuel and some weapons) are in the Shipyard panel, under Replenishment (their card says what each carries). In a friendly port they load from its stock, never taking it below half of what it should hold.
texts.guideTanker: Your side has no tanker aircraft: the game has no Soviet or Chinese tanker of 1985 (the enemy keeps a KC-10A Extender at NAF Atsugi). How a tanker works:
texts.guideExampleStrike: The four H-6Ds at Shanghai-Dachang with a Strike loadout on Ching Chuan Kang before the Tsoying landing: fewer fighters to meet your landing ships.
texts.guideExampleSupply: Tsoying, once taken, is the next base to be fought for: set it to High so its missiles are topped up before the counter-attack comes.
texts.guideExampleIntel: "A satellite pass at 0456Z shows about 6 surface ships 140 nm from Yokosuka": the red circle on the map is that area, not a firm position.
texts.guideCarrierPrices: Their price in the Shipyard panel. Carriers by tier: Moskva 300, Kiev 750, Orel 1,300. A Kiev or Orel of yours costs 10 % less and joins with all its helicopters and 30 % of each fixed-wing type; a Moskva joins whole at full price.
texts.guideVictory: The first side to hold every base in the theatre but those on the enemy's home soil wins: for you, everything outside mainland Australia and Hawaii (Pearl Harbor and Hickam), Japan, Guam and Port Moresby included; for the enemy, everything outside the Russian and Chinese mainland, islands included (Sakhalin, Hainan, Zhoushan...).
texts.guideRoad: Tsoying first (it brings Ching Chuan Kang with it), then White Beach and Kadena, then Chinhae; then Subic Bay (a naval base, held by 3 battalions) with Clark, and last the south: Singapore, Malaya and the Indonesian ports. Then Japan.
texts.guideReplenStart: Your side starts with none: order a Kazbek or a Boris Chilikin.
texts.guideBatteries: (Soviet: Rubezh and Redut; China: HY-2 and HY-1; the enemy's US and Japanese bases M110 and M109 guns, Australia's M109, its allies' M110 or M109)
texts.guideSams: (Soviet: SA-3, SA-8; China: SA-2 for its HQ-2; the enemy's US: Nike Hercules; Japan: Nike Hercules, Type 81; Australia, Singapore and Indonesia: Rapier; Korea: Vulcan guns, Malaysia: M42 guns, Taiwan: GDF guns, in place of SAM sites)
texts.guideEnemy: It starts on a peacetime footing, 54 ships nearly all in port: Midway at Yokosuka, Constellation at Subic Bay, the amphibious group at White Beach, the Japanese and Australians at home, two Taiwanese submarines at Tsoying; only two attack submarines are out. Its landings come one at a time: to take back White Beach, Tsoying, Chinhae, Subic Bay and Singapore, and for Korsakov and Cam Ranh Bay.
texts.guideSamReach: Nike Hercules 70 nm, SA-2 and HQ-2 25, SA-3 15, SA-8 6, Type 81 5, Rapier 4
texts.endingWon: The last base the enemy held beyond Australia and Hawaii has fallen. The American fleet is back behind its own coasts, and the Western Pacific is ours. The war is won.
texts.endingLost: The enemy holds every base we had beyond the Russian and Chinese mainland. What is left of the fleets has fallen back to Vladivostok and the Chinese ports. The war is lost.
texts.procurementLift: a place in a landing ship (Ivan Rogov, Ropucha, Alligator and Yukan 2 each · the enemy's Tarawa 3, Austin 2, Charleston or Newport 1)
texts.messageVictory: Victory. Every base outside the enemy's home soil{besides} is ours: the campaign is won.
texts.messageDefeat: Defeat. {winner} holds every base outside our home soil{besides}: the campaign is lost.
texts.sitrepNote: The clock is paused: Space starts it
texts.sitrepNoteTip: Press Space, or Play in the time controls (top right), to start the clock. New to the campaign? The Guide (the book at the bottom of the left strip) starts with your first hour.

situation: As of 0000Z the Soviet Union and the People's Republic of China are at war with the United States, Japan and their allies in the Pacific. No declaration has been made: the enemy has had no warning beyond what his own intelligence made of our exercises.

The war plan of the Main Naval Staff is now in force: Taiwan first, then Okinawa, then South Korea; then the Philippines, and last Singapore, Malaya and the Indonesian islands. Taken quickly, they give us the island chain and the straits before America can reinforce across the Pacific.
The north is the Pacific Fleet's, with the North and East Sea Fleets of the PLA Navy. The south is run from Cam Ranh Bay, where our squadron and the South Sea Fleet are to close the South China Sea.
Supply comes from Vladivostok, Shanghai and Cam Ranh Bay. Every port we take must be fed by convoy until it can feed the next landing.
enemy: The enemy is on a peacetime footing. The Seventh Fleet is in harbour: the carrier Midway at Yokosuka, Constellation at Subic Bay, the amphibious group at White Beach. The Japanese escort flotillas lie in their home ports. Expect him to wake quickly, and to answer first from the air, from Kadena, Misawa and Clark.
The allied garrisons on Taiwan, in Korea and in the south are light and short of stocks. The American bases on Okinawa and in the Philippines are better found.
Once roused, he will bring his carriers against our landings and run his convoys from Pearl Harbor under escort. His patrol aircraft will look for our submarines, his ships and submarines hunt them.
intent: Take Tsoying, then Okinawa. The landing forces are at sea and loaded: every hour the enemy has to prepare is against us.
Strike the enemy's airfields before each landing goes in, and keep the escorts close round the landing ships.
Our submarines across the Pacific are to attack enemy shipping and report every movement from Pearl Harbor and Guam. The missile submarines stay in the Okhotsk bastion.
Preserve the carriers, keep the sea lanes open, and be ready for the American counter-stroke.

firstOrder.title: Raid the lanes into Yokosuka
firstOrder.briefing: Midway's group and the escorts at Yokosuka are fed by the American trunk lane from Pearl Harbor, which passes to the south of you on its way to the mouth of Tokyo Bay. Get onto it and sink the shipping bound for Yokosuka within 4 days, before the enemy can put escorts round his convoys. Expect patrol aircraft from Misawa and destroyers out of Yokosuka: attack out at sea, not off the bay.

starts.name: South China Sea, off Cam Ranh

firstOrder.title: Raid the lanes into Singapore
firstOrder.briefing: Singapore is the last objective of the war plan, and it is supplied by sea from Subic Bay, across the South China Sea. Start starving it now: sink the shipping bound for Singapore within 5 days. Constellation is still alongside at Subic Bay, but once she sails her aircraft can reach the lane, so strike early and keep moving.

firstOrder.title: Cover the Hainan lane
firstOrder.briefing: The South Sea Fleet's feeder lane from Zhanjiang to Yulin carries the stores for Yulin and Lingshui, and it will be the first of our lanes the Americans go for when Constellation sails from Subic Bay. Send patrol aircraft out on the mission Cover a lane (MISSION, Escort and cover) over it off Yulin and keep the lane watched for 12 hours in all within 2 days; fighters cannot cover a lane. Report every contact to the South Sea Fleet.

firstOrder.title: Secure the Vladivostok approaches
firstOrder.briefing: Every group that sails from Vladivostok must cross these approaches, and at least one American submarine is believed to be in the Sea of Japan. Keep a ship of yours at sea within 30 nm of Vladivostok for 12 hours in all within 2 days. Report any contact at once.

starts.name: Taiwan Strait, off the Penghu Islands

firstOrder.title: Cover the Tsoying landing
firstOrder.briefing: The South Sea Fleet's landing squadron is a few hours off Tsoying with only the East Sea Fleet's destroyers round it, and the Nationalist fighters at Ching Chuan Kang will come at it as soon as the enemy wakes. Take station within 40 nm of the landing area west of Tsoying and keep a ship there for 24 hours in all within 2 days. Until Tsoying falls, your ships are the landing's air defence.

firstOrder.title: Bar the Jeju Strait
firstOrder.briefing: Korea is the war plan's third objective, and before our landing goes in the Japanese escort flotilla at Sasebo will try to reach the Yellow Sea through the Jeju Strait. Shut that door: keep a ship of yours within 40 nm of the strait between Jeju and the Korean coast for 18 hours in all within 3 days. The Japanese fighters on Kyushu can reach you there; keep your air defence closed up.

firstOrder.title: Picket Constellation's road north
firstOrder.briefing: If Constellation sails from Subic Bay to break up the Tsoying landing, her shortest road north runs up the west coast of Luzon. Take station within 50 nm of the point off north-western Luzon and keep a ship there for 18 hours in all within 3 days; it is a long run from the Paracels, so start now. The fighters at Clark reach you there: a picket that reports her and lives is worth more than one that fights.

firstOrder.title: Cover the strait lane
firstOrder.briefing: Our coastal trunk lane through the Taiwan Strait carries the South Sea Fleet's stores from Shanghai, and it passes within easy reach of Taiwan's F-5s at Ching Chuan Kang. Put patrol aircraft on the mission Cover a lane (MISSION, Escort and cover) over it off the Fujian coast and keep them on station for 18 hours in all within 2 days. Only patrol aircraft can cover a lane; your fighters can keep the Nationalists off them.

firstOrder.title: Close the Bashi Channel
firstOrder.briefing: The Bashi Channel is the short way from Subic Bay to the waters east of Taiwan and on to Okinawa, for Constellation and for the American convoys alike. Take your boat south and keep within 30 nm of the channel, between Taiwan and the Batanes, for 24 hours in all within 3 days. Expect American patrol aircraft over the channel once the landing at Tsoying is reported.

firstOrder.title: Raid the Balikpapan oil run
firstOrder.briefing: Balikpapan's oil terminal is fed by the American lane from Subic Bay, which comes down the northern Makassar Strait from the Celebes Sea and passes some 90 nm north of you on its way in. Sink the shipping bound for Balikpapan within 5 days. Little hunts submarines in these waters yet, but every attack gives the enemy a datum: shift your ground after each one.
